record.title: Skouw suspends border services for presidential inauguration ceremony
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Skouw land crossing services at the Indonesia–PNG frontier
record.direction: Arrival and departure processing described; category-specific implementation not separately observed.
record.movement: Ordinary users of crossing services; the report discusses passport and traditional border-pass processing.
record.imposing_authority: Indonesian Skouw border administration; suspension reported by Papua provincial border bureau
record.enforcement: A named border official confirmed no service that day and notification to PNG.
record.consequences: Temporary loss of ordinary crossing services; quantified economic effects not established.
record.relationship: Distinct from Skouw security closures in 2019 and COVID restrictions in EA018.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred
record.official_rationale: Papua border bureau head Suzana Wanggai attributed May 9 service suspension to the presidential inauguration ceremony for the Skouw facility; Papua New Guinea had been notified.
record.context: Authorities suspended ordinary crossing services for the inauguration of the refurbished border post. This is a deliberate administrative suspension, not a closure inferred from construction work.
record.uncertainty: One principal closure-reporting origin. The inauguration speech corroborates the ceremony, not resumption of traffic. Exact hours, exemptions and reopening date remain unverified.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Contemporaneous official interview states no border services that day and notice to PNG.
No exact resumption is stated; the inauguration itself is not an endpoint.

Hierarchical coding review: Known reason outside taxonomy. The ceremony explains the suspension but sits outside the rationale taxonomy. It is distinguished from an unknown reason. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Ceremony is the reason given, with no supported six-code rationale.
Skouw processing for border-pass and passport travellers; no broader frontier claim.
Unknown actual end prevents exact duration.
